reply.english: There are five people in my family.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: كَمْ فَرْدًا فِي عَائِلَتِكِ يَا مُنَى؟
dialogue.english: How many people are in your family, Muna?

dialogue.speaker: Muna
dialogue.arabic: فِي عَائِلَتِي سِتَّةُ أَفْرَاد: أَبِي وَأُمِّي وَثَلَاثَةُ إِخْوَة وَأَنَا.
dialogue.transliteration: fee 3aa2ilatee sittatu afraad: abee wa ummee wa thalaathatu ikhwa wa anaa.
dialogue.english: There are six people in my family: my father, my mother, three brothers and me.

dialogue.speaker: Muna
dialogue.english: And are you married?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: لَا، مَا زِلْتُ أَعْزَب. وَأَنْتِ، هَلْ أَنْتِ مُتَزَوِّجَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: laa, maa ziltu a3zab. wa anti, hal anti mutazawwija?
dialogue.english: No, I'm still single. And you, are you married?

dialogue.speaker: Muna
dialogue.english: Yes, my husband is an engineer.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: Do you have children?

dialogue.speaker: Muna
dialogue.english: Yes, I have a son and a daughter.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: مَا شَاءَ اللَّه! مَا اسْمُ اِبْنِكِ؟
dialogue.transliteration: maa shaa2a allaah! maa ismu ibnik?
dialogue.english: Wonderful! What's your son's name?

dialogue.speaker: Muna
dialogue.english: His name is Omar, and my daughter's name is Sara.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: I wish them all the best.

dialogue.speaker: Muna
dialogue.english: Thank you, Khalid.

pair.english: How many people are in your family? (to a man)

response.english: There are five people in my family.
Yes, my husband is a doctor.

pair.english: Do you have brothers and sisters? (to a man)

response.english: I have a brother and two sisters.

lessons.culture: In Fusha a family member is named with a possessive ending, so the ending ـِي means 'my' and أُمِّي is 'my mother'. Asking whether someone is married changes for a man and a woman, and it is polite to ask only once you know the person a little.

exercises.prompt: A colleague asks you: 'هَلْ أَنْتَ مُتَزَوِّج؟' Say you are still single.
exercises.tip: مَا زِلْتُ means 'I am still'; add the state after it.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: 'كَمْ فَرْدًا فِي عَائِلَتِكَ؟' Say there are five.
exercises.tip: فَرْد is one person; أَفْرَاد is the plural.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'لِي أَخٌ وَ_____.' (I have a brother and two sisters.)
exercises.tip: The ending ـَانِ marks exactly two.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'هَلْ أَنْتِ _____؟' (Are you married? to a woman)
exercises.tip: The ending ـَة makes the word feminine.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I have a son and a daughter.'
exercises.tip: لَدَيَّ means 'I have', like لِي.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Are you married?' (to a woman)
exercises.tip: هَلْ opens a yes-or-no question.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'my sister'?
exercises.tip: أُخْت is sister, أَخ is brother.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks a man whether he is married?
exercises.tip: أَنْتَ is for a man, أَنْتِ for a woman.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'أَنْتَ / مُتَزَوِّج / هَلْ'.
exercises.tip: هَلْ always comes first.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'فِي / عَائِلَتِي / أَفْرَاد / خَمْسَةُ'.
exercises.tip: Start with فِي عَائِلَتِي, 'in my family'.

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.english: I'm very hungry.

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.transliteration: wa anaa aydan. ureedu an aakul.
dialogue.english: Me too. I want to eat.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.english: Welcome. What would you like?

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.arabic: أُحِبُّ الْفَلَافِل. وَمَاذَا تُحِبِّين يَا نُورَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: u7ibbu al-falaafil. wa maathaa tu7ibbeen yaa Noora?
dialogue.english: I like falafel. And what do you like, Nora?

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.english: I want chicken with rice.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.english: And what will you drink?

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا عَطْشَانَة. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْرَبَ الْمَاء.
dialogue.english: I'm thirsty. I want to drink water.

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.english: And I want coffee.

dialogue.speaker: Jamal
dialogue.english: Right away. Here you are, enjoy your meal.

dialogue.speaker: Adel
dialogue.english: Thank you. Join us.

pair.english: What do you like to eat?

lessons.culture: In Fusha people say هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا to someone who is eating and صِحَّةً وَعَافِيَة after a drink, and the host often answers تَفَضَّلْ مَعَنَا, an invitation to join. Sharing food is a sign of hospitality across the Arab world.

exercises.prompt: A waiter asks: 'مَاذَا تُحِبُّ أَنْ تَأْكُل؟' Say you like falafel.
exercises.tip: أُحِبُّ means 'I like'; the food follows it.

exercises.prompt: Someone starts eating near you. Wish them a good meal.
exercises.tip: It is said to a person while they eat.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'أُرِيدُ أَنْ _____ الْمَاء.' (I want to drink water.)
exercises.tip: After أَنْ the verb ends with a fatha sound.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'أَنَا _____ جِدًّا.' (I'm very hungry, a woman speaking.)
exercises.tip: The ending ـَة makes the word feminine.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'The bill, please.'
exercises.tip: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ means 'please'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I want to eat.'
exercises.tip: أُرِيدُ أَنْ is 'I want to'.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'thirsty' (said by a man)?
exercises.tip: عَطْشَان is thirsty; جَائِع is hungry.

exercises.prompt: What do you say to someone who has just finished drinking?
exercises.tip: هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا is for someone still eating.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'أَنْ / أُرِيدُ / آكُل'.
exercises.tip: Start with أُرِيدُ, 'I want'.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'هُوَ / كَمْ / الْحِسَاب'.
exercises.tip: كَمْ, 'how much', opens the question.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: How old are you, Khalid?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: I am thirty. And you?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا فِي الْخَامِسَةِ وَالْعِشْرِين. هَلْ أَنْتَ مُتَزَوِّج؟
dialogue.transliteration: anaa fee al-khaamisati wal-3ishreen. hal anta mutazawwij?
dialogue.english: I am twenty-five. Are you married?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, anaa mutazawwij wa ladayya tiflaan.
dialogue.english: Yes, I am married and I have two children.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: Masha Allah. Where does your family live?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: نَسْكُنُ فِي جُدَّة. وَأَخِي الْأَكْبَر فِي الرِّيَاض.
dialogue.transliteration: naskunu fee Judda. wa akhee al-akbar fee ar-riyaad.
dialogue.english: We live in Jeddah. And my older brother is in Riyadh.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: What does your brother do?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: هُوَ طَبِيب. هُوَ طَوِيل وَمَرِح جِدًّا.
dialogue.transliteration: huwa tabeeb. huwa taweel wa mari7 jiddan.
dialogue.english: He is a doctor. He is tall and very funny.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: And your sister?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.english: My younger sister is kind. She is a student.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.transliteration: wa hal jadduka wa jaddatuka ma3akum?
dialogue.english: And are your grandparents with you?

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.transliteration: na3am, jaddee wa jaddatee yaskunaani ma3anaa.
dialogue.english: Yes, my grandparents live with us.

lessons.culture: Fusha has separate words for each relative: عَمّ is a father's brother and خَال a mother's brother, so اِبْنُ عَمِّي and اِبْنُ خَالِي are different cousins. It is polite to answer a mention of someone's children with مَاشَاءَ اللَّه.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: 'كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟' Say you are thirty years old.
exercises.tip: عُمْرِي means 'my age'; the number follows.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: 'مَاذَا تَعْمَلُ؟' Say you are an engineer.
exercises.tip: No verb 'to be' is needed: أَنَا مُهَنْدِس.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'هِيَ _____ جِدًّا.' (She is very kind.)
exercises.tip: With هِيَ the describing word takes ة.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'لَدَيَّ _____.' (I have two children.)
exercises.tip: The ending ـان makes it 'two'.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'My cousin is funny.'
exercises.tip: Start with the person, then the describing word.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'I am married.' (a man speaking)
exercises.tip: A woman would say مُتَزَوِّجَة.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'tall'?
exercises.tip: طَوِيل is tall; قَصِير is short.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase means 'my younger sister'?
exercises.tip: الصُّغْرَى is younger, الْكُبْرَى is older.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'تَسْكُنُ / أَيْنَ / عَائِلَتُكَ'.
exercises.tip: The question word أَيْنَ comes first.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'جِدًّا / طَوِيل / هُوَ'.
exercises.tip: جِدًّا, 'very', goes after the word it strengthens.

reply.english: We will eat rice and fish.

dialogue.speaker: Mother
dialogue.arabic: الْفَطُورُ عَلَى السَّاعَةِ الثَّامِنَة يَا أَحْمَد.
dialogue.english: Breakfast is at eight, Ahmad.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.arabic: حَسَنًا يَا أُمِّي. مَاذَا سَنَأْكُلُ عَلَى الْغَدَاء؟
dialogue.english: All right, Mum. What are we eating for lunch?

dialogue.speaker: Mother
dialogue.arabic: سَنَأْكُلُ الْأَرُزَّ وَالسَّمَك. سَاعِدْنِي فِي الطَّبْخ.
dialogue.transliteration: sana2kulu al-aruzza was-samak. saa3idnee fee at-tabkh.
dialogue.english: We will eat rice and fish. Help me cook.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: Gladly. Shall I set the table?

dialogue.speaker: Mother
dialogue.english: Yes, set the table. The food is ready.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: Pass me the salt, please.

dialogue.speaker: Father
dialogue.arabic: هَذَا لَذِيذ جِدًّا. شُكْرًا يَا أُمَّ أَحْمَد.
dialogue.transliteration: haathaa ladheedh jiddan. shukran yaa umma A7mad.
dialogue.english: This is very delicious. Thank you, Umm Ahmad.

dialogue.speaker: Mother
dialogue.english: More?

dialogue.speaker: Father
dialogue.english: More, please.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: I am full, thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Mother
dialogue.arabic: اِرْفَعِ الْمَائِدَة يَا أَحْمَد، وَالْعَشَاءُ فِي التَّاسِعَة.
dialogue.transliteration: irfa3i al-maa2ida yaa A7mad, wal-3ashaa2u fee at-taasi3a.
dialogue.english: Clear the table, Ahmad, and dinner is at nine.

dialogue.speaker: Ahmad
dialogue.english: As you wish, Mum.

pair.english: What are we eating for lunch?

response.english: We will eat rice and fish.
No, thank you, I am full.
No, I do not eat meat.

lessons.culture: A Fusha-speaking host often keeps offering more food, and the guest says أَنَا شَبْعَان, 'I am full', after one or two polite refusals. The family usually eats from shared dishes on one table, so asking someone to pass something uses نَاوِلْنِي.

exercises.prompt: Your mother asks: 'الْمَزِيدَ؟' Politely say you want more.
exercises.tip: مِنْ فَضْلِكِ ends in kasra when speaking to a woman.

exercises.prompt: A guest offers you meat. Say you do not eat meat.
exercises.tip: لَا before the verb means 'I do not'.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'الطَّعَامُ _____.' (The food is ready.)
exercises.tip: جَاهِز describes الطَّعَام.

exercises.prompt: Complete: 'نَاوِلْنِي _____.' (Pass me the salt.)
exercises.tip: نَاوِلْنِي is 'pass me' (to a man).

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'This is delicious.'
exercises.tip: لَذِيذ is the Fusha word for delicious.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Fusha: 'Help me cook.' (to a man)
exercises.tip: فِي links the help to the task.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'full' (after eating, said by a man)?
exercises.tip: شَبْعَان is full; جَائِع is hungry.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase means 'Dinner is at nine'?
exercises.tip: الْعَشَاء is dinner; الْفَطُور is breakfast.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'الْمَائِدَة / جَهِّزِ'.
exercises.tip: The command comes first.

exercises.prompt: Put these words in order: 'جَاهِز / الطَّعَامُ'.
exercises.tip: Name the thing first, then say it is ready.

challenge.title: A family meal
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation in Fusha in which two people talk about their families over a meal, say what they like to eat and drink, and ask for the bill.
required_elements: how many people are in each family
a brother or sister and whether one is married
what each person likes to eat
a wish for a good meal
the bill asked for and its price

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.arabic: كَمْ فَرْدًا فِي عَائِلَتِكَ يَا فَهْد؟
dialogue.english: How many people are in your family, Fahd?

dialogue.speaker: Fahd
dialogue.arabic: فِي عَائِلَتِي أَرْبَعَةُ أَفْرَاد. لِي أُخْتٌ وَاحِدَة، وَهِيَ مُتَزَوِّجَة.
dialogue.transliteration: fee 3aa2ilatee arba3atu afraad. lee ukhtun waa7ida, wa hiya mutazawwija.
dialogue.english: There are four people in my family. I have one sister, and she is married.

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.arabic: أَنَا جَائِعَة. مَاذَا تُحِبُّ أَنْ تَأْكُل؟
dialogue.transliteration: anaa jaa2i3a. maathaa tu7ibbu an ta2kul?
dialogue.english: I'm hungry. What do you like to eat?

dialogue.speaker: Fahd
dialogue.arabic: أُحِبُّ الْفَلَافِل، وَأُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْرَبَ شَاي.
dialogue.transliteration: u7ibbu al-falaafil, wa ureedu an ashraba shaay.
dialogue.english: I like falafel, and I want to drink tea.

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.english: And I want coffee.

dialogue.speaker: Fahd
dialogue.english: Enjoy your meal.

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.arabic: شُكْرًا، تَفَضَّلْ مَعَنَا. الْحِسَابَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
dialogue.transliteration: shukran, tafaddal ma3anaa. al-7isaaba min fadlika.
dialogue.english: Thank you, join us. The bill, please.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: The bill is thirty riyals.
